articles.title: Explanation of zodiac signs in astrology - Báo Nghệ An
articles.author: Báo Nghệ An
articles.content: Lý giải về cung hoàng đạo trong chiêm tinh học The zodiac is determined by the position of the Sun in the sky relative to the 12 constellations and is closely related to astrology. | The 12 zodiac signs are linked to the Earth's movement across the sky. Photo: Wordpress. |  The zodiac, or the 12 signs listed in astrology, are linked to the Earth's movement across the sky. Because the Earth revolves around the Sun on a plane, we see the Sun appear and move in front of different constellations throughout the year, according to Earth Sky. Just as the Moon appears in a slightly different position in the sky each night, the Sun's position relative to distant background stars gradually shifts eastward from day to day. For example, if the Sun is in Gemini this month, it will be in Cancer next month. The specific dates listed in Western astrology are used to identify when the Sun is in a particular zodiac sign. For example, March 21st to April 19th is the sign of Aries. Nowadays, the zodiac sign you were born in does not necessarily coincide with the name of the constellation the Sun is passing through. To understand why constellations no longer correspond to their respective zodiac signs, we need to know more about how the Earth moves. The Earth rotates, and its North Pole doesn't always point in the same direction. Like a spinning top, the Earth wobbles, causing the North Pole to move in a circle across the celestial sphere. This wobble is quite slow, with a cycle of 26,000 years, meaning the Earth doesn't actually complete a full orbit in a year. After about 2,000 years, the Sun will be in a completely different constellation for the same period of time. On the summer solstice in June 2,000 years ago, the Sun was almost directly between the constellations Gemini and Cancer. But on the summer solstice of 2016, the Sun was between Gemini and Taurus. In the year 4609, the Sun will leave Taurus and move to Aries on the summer solstice. The zodiac signs, corresponding to the constellations through which the Sun passes, were determined 2,000 years ago. However, by the mid-21st century, the slow wobble of the Earth's rotational axis caused the summer solstice, winter solstice, and spring and autumn equinoxes to shift approximately 30 degrees westward relative to the constellations. Currently, the zodiac signs and constellations are out of alignment by about a month. In about 2,000 years, they will be out of alignment by about two months. The constellations of the zodiac are not all the same size and shape. Most of them appear in the texts of the ancient Babylonians and were introduced by Ptolemy, the Greek astronomer who lived in the 2nd century. In 1930, the International Astronomical Union defined the boundaries of modern constellations, encompassing all 13 constellations that lie along the path of the Sun. The constellation not listed in Western astrology is Ophiuchus, located between Sagittarius and Scorpio. According to VNE | RELATED NEWS |  |---|

articles.title: Potentially habitable planet near Earth discovered. - Vietnam.vn
articles.author: Báo Khoa học và Đời sống
articles.content: Astronomers have identified a potential candidate for habitable planet, HD 137010 b. This planet orbits a sun-like star and is estimated to be about 6% larger than Earth. Image: NASA. A team of international scientists from Australia, the UK, the US, and Denmark discovered the planet HD 137010 b by examining and analyzing data recorded in 2017 from the K2 expansion mission of the Kepler space telescope of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). Image: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Keith Miller (Caltech/IPAC). Dr. Chelsea Huang, a researcher at the University of Southern Queensland (Australia) and one of the study's co-authors, said that HD 137010 b has an orbital period similar to Earth's, completing one rotation in approximately 355 days. (Image: Eckhard Slawik/Science Photo Library/Getty Images) Researchers predict that planet HD 137010 b has "about a 50% chance of being within the habitable zone" of its central star. Image: NASA/JPL-Caltech. You may also like "What's incredibly interesting about this Earth-sized planet is that its star system is only about 150 light-years from our Solar System," Dr. Huang said. Photo: NASA/JPL-Caltech. According to Dr. Huang, the planet with the greatest potential for extraterrestrial life after HD 137010 b is Kepler-186f. However, Kepler-186f is four times farther away and its central star is 20 times dimmer. Image: NASA/JPL-Caltech. While transiting in front of its central star, the planet HD 137010 b was discovered by a team of citizen scientists, including the lead author of the study, Dr. Alexander Venner, when he was still a high school student. Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, Joseph Olmsted (STScI). "It's truly a wonderful experience to return to this work and make such an important discovery ," Dr. Venner shared. Photo: NASA/JPL-Caltech. You may also like The host star of HD 137010 b is cooler and dimmer than the Sun. This means the planet's surface is likely similar to Mars and could have temperatures below -70 degrees Celsius. Image: NASA/JPL-Caltech. Readers are invited to watch the video: A map of the universe with over 900,000 stars, galaxies, and black holes. Source: THĐT1.

articles.author: Trọng Nhân
articles.content: The mystery of the smallest planet in the Solar System. Mercury is the first planet from the sun, and also the smallest of the eight "siblings" in the Solar System. There are many interesting things about this planet that scientists are currently studying. Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System family - Photo: Theosophy online The planet with the most iron in the solar system. Mercury is one of four rocky planets like Earth, and also the smallest, with a diameter of only about 4,879.4 km. This figure is 0.383 times the diameter of the Earth and is even smaller than Jupiter's moon Ganymede and Saturn's moon Titan. Iron makes up a large proportion of Mercury's composition. It is also the planet with the most iron in the Solar System. Along with Venus, Mercury has no natural satellites, while the other planets all have satellites orbiting them. The diurnal temperature range is approximately 600 degrees Celsius. Mercury's atmosphere is extremely thin - Photo: NASA Mercury is also the closest planet to the sun among the eight planets, at a distance of approximately 57.91 million kilometers. This, along with its small mass, makes its atmosphere very thin and unable to retain heat. Therefore, Mercury has the largest diurnal temperature range in the Solar System, with nighttime temperatures dropping to -173°C but daytime temperatures reaching 427°C. This translates to a temperature difference of up to 600°C between day and night. Due to its very thin atmosphere, Mercury does not have seasons like the four seasons on Earth. Mercury's orbit is an extremely narrow ellipse with a major axis radius of 70 million km and a minor axis radius of only 46 million km. This is also one of the reasons for the large temperature differences on Mercury. A day is equal to two-thirds of a year. A year on Mercury is equivalent to only 88 days on Earth - Photo: NASA Mercury orbits the sun at a very fast rate, approximately 88 Earth days. In contrast, Mercury takes about 58 Earth days to rotate on its axis. Thus, a year on Mercury is incredibly fast, only 88 days compared to 365 days on our planet, while a single day is incredibly long, equivalent to about two Earth months. In other words, a day on Mercury is about two-thirds the length of a year. The surface is like the moon. Mercury's surface is uneven, like the moon. Photo: NASA Bề mặt sao Thủy có rất nhiều hố to nhỏ và lởm chởm như bề mặt mặt trăng. Phần lớn bề mặt sao Thủy được dung nham khô bao phủ. Trên bề mặt hành tinh này xuất hiện nhiều vết nứt, hoặc những vách đá khổng lồ kéo dài trên một khu vực rộng lớn, trông giống các nấc thang khổng lồ. Trong đó, nấc lớn nhất dài hơn 1.000km và cao đến 3km. Sao Thủy có lượng lớn miệng núi lửa trên bề mặt hơn bất kỳ hành tinh nào trong Hệ mặt trời. Điều đặc biệt là phần lớn các miệng núi lửa này được đặt tên theo các nhà văn, nghệ sĩ nổi tiếng. "Thần đưa tin" của Hệ mặt trời Thần Hermes trong thần thoại Hy Lạp Con người biết đến sao Thủy từ rất sớm. 3.000 năm TCN, người Sume đã biết có sự hiện diện của sao Thủy. Vì sao Thủy nằm trong quỹ đạo Trái đất nên khi nhìn từ Trái đất chỉ có thể thấy vào rạng sáng hoặc chiều tối chứ không thể thấy vào ban đêm. Người La Mã lấy tên thần Mercurius (người Hi Lạp gọi là thần Hermes) - vị thần liên lạc và đưa tin trong thần thoại, đặt cho sao Thủy. Có lẽ do người La Mã nhận thấy tốc độ nhanh của sao Thủy nên đặt tên như thế. Rất khó "làm quen" Vệ tinh Messenger đã hoàn thành nhiệm vụ vào năm 2015. Ảnh: NASA Our understanding of Mercury remains limited due to the difficulty in accessing the planet. To date, only two probes have attempted to reach Mercury: Mariner 10 in 1974-1975, and Messenger, launched into space on August 3, 2004. As for the Messenger spacecraft, after arriving in Mercury's orbit on March 17, 2011, it carried out the mission of observing and studying the history and geology of the planet, which is closest to the sun. Messenger traveled 7.8 billion kilometers over more than six years to reach Mercury and was the first spacecraft to successfully enter Mercury's orbit. Messenger orbited Mercury from 2011-2015 and sent back more than 280,000 images to Earth before ending its mission by crashing into the planet.

articles.title: Why in the world only 4 countries can produce ballpoint pens? - xaluannews.com
articles.author: Xã Luận Tin Nóng
articles.content: Ballpoint pens are familiar and common items in our daily lives. The reason why it is called a ballpoint pen is because the nib has a small part that is a ball that has the function of pushing the ink contained in the pen to the outside. A special thing is that almost every country has its own brand of ballpoint pens, but there are only 4 countries in the world that can produce ballpoint pen tips. This ball is small but plays an important role, it rotates freely to allow ink to flow evenly with each pen stroke. Producing a spinning iron ball that can write comfortably for a long time is not a simple thing, but requires a very high level of engineering. Machining accuracy is 1/1000 mm. The error is not allowed to exceed 0.003 mm. Besides the way the small marble is made, the material is also a very important factor. The steel used to manufacture this ball must be a special material - Tungsten carbide has twice the hardness of steel. Therefore, this is also known as one of the most difficult details in the world. Currently, only Switzerland, Germany, Japan and, more recently, China hold the technology of producing ballpoint pen tips. So why in the world only 4 countries can produce this "micro" part? Switzerland and Germany are two rich and developed countries. At the same time, it is famous for its precision, fine and quality machinery manufacturing techniques. Of the four countries, Switzerland is the most "skilled" producer of ballpoint pens. The Swiss company takes more than 20 stages to produce a small ballpoint pen with strict requirements: Processing accuracy must reach 1/1000 mm; The tip of the pen has 5 ink channels; The match between the ball, the pen tip and the groove position should not exceed 3 microns, and the thickness at the top of the pen tip is only 0.3-0.4 mm. As an island nation, lacking resources, having to import many things from outside, Japan’s manufacturing industry is very strong and developed, ranked first in the world. With modern scientific and technological applications, ballpoint pens are produced exclusively by Japan throughout Asia. By 2017, China became the fourth country to be able to produce this part. According to China Daily , before that, the country of billions of people produced 38 billion ballpoint pens per year, this number accounts for about 80% of the total number of ballpoint pens in the world. There are more than 3,000 pen manufacturing companies in this country, but none have the advanced technology to produce ballpoint pen tips. Instead, about 90% of the tips are imported from Japan, Germany and Switzerland. According to the China Light Industry Council, this costs the industry $17.3 million a year. After relentless research, China has mastered the ballpoint pen manufacturing technology and now accounts for 80% of the country’s ballpoint pen market. Nearly 40 billion ballpoint pens are produced in a year. In addition to the level of science and technology, the problem of profit also makes few countries invest in the production of this product. The daily output of the iron and steel mill can be equal to the steel consumed by the pen industry in a year. A ballpoint pen on the market can only sell for a few dollars, the profit is not high. Therefore, steel mills in many countries are not unable to produce ballpoint pens, but facing the problem of profit, they do not choose to spend money on research and development of this product. Source: General: washingtonpos; craftpaperie; jingdapen

articles.title: A 'second moon' briefly visited Earth. - Vietnam.vn
articles.author: Báo Tiền Phong
articles.content: Although it may appear to be a "second moon" of Earth, this is not a true satellite. It is expected to escape Earth's gravitational influence in early December 2026 and return to orbit around the Sun. The Minor Planet Center (MPC), an agency of the International Astronomical Union (IAU), said that this asteroid, designated "2026 QQ8", has been held in place by Earth's gravity since April. This asteroid is a small celestial body, with a diameter of only about 2 meters. It is predicted to remain near Earth until early December, before moving out of our planet's gravitational field and returning to its orbit around the Sun. "2026,QQ8" was first discovered last August by Hungarian astronomer Krisztián Sárneczky. Initially, it was thought to be a regular asteroid, but precise orbital calculations have revealed that it is now staying close to Earth. You may also like Analyses indicate there is no risk of collision with Earth. Even if it were to enter the atmosphere, given its small size, it would almost certainly be burned up completely. Such instances, where Earth's gravity temporarily holds a small asteroid in place, are not uncommon. Matthew Payne, director of the Minor Planet Center (MPC), explained: "It is entirely possible that such an object exists near Earth at any given time," adding that they typically remain there for a few weeks or months. You may also like There have been instances in the past where asteroids were temporarily trapped by Earth's gravity. Asteroid 2006 RH120 was near Earth for about a year, while 2020 CD3 orbited our planet for about three years. Astronomers believe that most asteroids observed near Earth originate from the asteroid belt located between Mars and Jupiter. The hypothesis is that the orbits of objects in this belt may be altered by gravitational forces, causing them to move closer to Earth. If their speed decreases sufficiently, they may be temporarily held in place by Earth's gravity. To date, astronomers have identified approximately 40,000 celestial objects in the vicinity of Earth. Across the entire solar system, about 1.5 million celestial objects have been identified.

articles.title: Why will August 2nd, 2027 be the most special day of the 21st century? - Vietnam.vn
articles.author: Báo Dân trí
articles.content: The "eclipse of the century" will occur on August 2, 2027. August 12th will be a highly anticipated day for many astronomy enthusiasts, as it marks the time of a total solar eclipse, when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun, forming a straight line, lasting for 2 minutes and 18 seconds. People living in Vietnam will not be able to observe this phenomenon. Only those living in northern Spain, a small part of Portugal , Iceland, Greenland, etc., will be able to observe the total solar eclipse. Meanwhile, those living in the Northern Hemisphere, including Northern Europe, Canada, and parts of the northern United States, will only be able to observe a partial solar eclipse. A total solar eclipse will not occur again until August 2, 2027. Notably, the eclipse that will happen next year is called the "eclipse of the century," when the Moon will completely obscure the Sun for 6 minutes and 23 seconds, the longest in the 21st century. This time is long enough for the corona (the outermost layer of the Sun's atmosphere) to shine brightly against the dark sky, and the stars will also shine as brightly as they do at night. Scientists say this record will not be broken until June 3, 2114, when a total solar eclipse will last for 6 minutes and 32 seconds. The total solar eclipse in 2027 is one of a series of three total solar eclipses occurring in three consecutive years (August 12, 2026, August 2, 2027, and July 22, 2028). This is also a very rare occurrence. You may also like Why will the total solar eclipse on August 2, 2027 last so long? The reason the total solar eclipse on August 2, 2027, will last longer is because this is when the Moon reaches its perigee, the point in its orbit where it is closest to Earth, making it appear larger when observed from the ground. Coincidentally, at this time, the Earth is also very close to its aphelion, the point where the Earth is farthest from the Sun, so the Sun will be obscured by the Moon for a longer period when observed from the ground. The shadow of the eclipse will also fall on the area near the Earth's equator, where the Earth rotates faster. This makes the eclipse last longer because the Earth's rotation speed catches up with the movement speed of the Moon and the Sun, helping to maintain a straight line between the three celestial bodies for a longer period. Is it possible to observe the solar eclipse on August 2, 2027, from Vietnam? The eclipse path on August 2, 2027, will begin over the Atlantic Ocean, then move across the Strait of Gibraltar, sweeping across southern Spain before moving into North Africa and the Middle East. Countries with the opportunity to observe this total solar eclipse include Spain, Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, and Somalia. Of these, the best location for observing the total solar eclipse for the longest period is the city of Luxor (Egypt). People living in Vietnam will not be able to observe the total solar eclipse on August 2, 2027, but those living in southern provinces and cities such as Ho Chi Minh City, Ca Mau , Can Tho, etc., will be able to observe a partial eclipse, with about 10% of the sun being obscured. However, the eclipse will occur around 6 PM (Vietnam time), making observation difficult. A total solar eclipse is a unique astronomical phenomenon that occurs when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun, forming a straight line. At this time, the Moon completely obscures the Sun. You may also like During a total solar eclipse, a dark area appears, a region where the Moon completely blocks sunlight from reaching the Earth. This dark area moves across the Earth's surface. People living within this dark area will be able to observe the total solar eclipse. A total solar eclipse is usually only visible for a few seconds to a maximum of 7.5 minutes, but often shorter than 3 minutes. Meanwhile, a partial or annular solar eclipse (where the Moon does not completely obscure the Sun) can last from a few minutes to several hours. According to NASA, the longest total solar eclipse ever recorded was 7 minutes and 28 seconds, occurring in 743 BC in the Indian Ocean. NASA predicts that on July 16, 2186, a total solar eclipse lasting up to 7 minutes and 29 seconds will occur over South American countries, especially Colombia, Venezuela, and Guyana.

articles.title: The diamond planet was once stripped of its atmosphere but regenerated it. - Vietnam.vn
articles.author: vietnam.vn
articles.content: According to a new report published in the journal Nature, researchers say the planet analyzed, named 55 Cancri e, is located about 41 light-years from Earth and is in the constellation Cancer. This planet is classified as a "super-Earth," with a diameter nearly twice that of Earth, while its mass is nine times that of Earth, Space.com quoted researcher Renyu Hu, a member of the astronomy team behind the new discovery and currently working at the California Institute of Technology (USA). The planet 55 Cancri e is only 2.3 million kilometers from its central star 55 Cancri A, taking approximately 17 Earth hours to complete an orbit around it. At this distance, Mercury, the planet closest to the sun, is still 25 times farther from the sun than the distance between 55 Cancri e and 55 Cancri A. The planet's extremely close proximity to its central star results in surface temperatures reaching 2,400 degrees Celsius.  Intense radiation from the central star blew away 55 Cancri e's original atmosphere, similar to other rocky planets that get too close to their stars. However, new research has discovered that the planet still has an atmosphere surrounding it. Thanks to the James Webb telescope, researchers discovered that 55 Cancri e possesses a thick atmosphere composed of carbon dioxide ( CO2 ) and carbon monoxide (CO), but their proportions are unknown. In contrast, Earth's atmosphere is composed of nitrogen, oxygen, argon, and other gases. What happened suggests that the planet successfully built a second atmosphere after its initial atmosphere was stripped away by its central star. The mechanism that allowed the planet to create this new atmosphere is currently unknown. Source: https://thanhnien.vn/hanh-tinh-kim-cuong-tung-bi-tuoc-mat-khi-quyen-nhung-tai-tao-cai-moi-185240510111933339.htm

articles.title: What would happen if the Earth stopped rotating? - Vietnam.vn
articles.author: Báo Dân trí
articles.content: (Dan Tri Newspaper) - If the Earth stopped rotating but continued to orbit the Sun, day and night could last for months, the climate would change drastically, posing major challenges to life on the planet. Astronomer Nikhita Ramkilowan at Rhodes University (South Africa) has provided interesting analyses of this hypothetical scenario. The Earth is like a giant sphere rotating on its axis, completing one revolution in about 24 hours. At the equator, the planet's surface moves at a speed of about 1,670 km/h. Humans don't perceive this movement because their bodies, the atmosphere, and the oceans all move with the Earth. The planet's rotation creates the day-night cycle and influences wind patterns and ocean currents. So what would happen if the Earth gradually slowed down and eventually stopped rotating on its axis, while still continuing to orbit the Sun? Day and night can last for months. If the Earth stopped rotating but continued to orbit the Sun, the day-night cycle at a given location would change dramatically. Instead of alternating between light and darkness every 24 hours, an area might experience about 6 months of light followed by about 6 months of darkness. This scenario doesn't mean half the Earth will permanently face the Sun while the other half remains in darkness. Because the planet continues to orbit the Sun, the regions alternate between illuminated and dark areas. In areas with long daylight hours, the surface absorbs heat for months at a time. Conversely, areas experiencing long nights lose heat, causing temperatures to drop sharply. These temperature differences can profoundly alter the climate and living conditions on the planet. Some areas located near the boundary between light and darkness may maintain relatively more stable light conditions. However, habitability in these areas depends on temperature, water availability, and other environmental factors. Weather and ocean conditions are changing drastically. You may also like The Earth's rotation creates the Coriolis effect, which causes air currents and ocean currents to be deflected as they move across the planet's surface. If the Earth stopped rotating, this effect would fundamentally change. Atmospheric and oceanic circulation systems would no longer function as they do today. Temperature differences between illuminated and long-term shadowed areas can alter wind direction, air circulation intensity, and global heat distribution. As a result, many areas may face extreme weather conditions, far different from the current climate. Life has been turned upside down. Many organisms have evolved to adapt to the day-night cycle. Plants use sunlight for photosynthesis, while some species regulate their flowering and growth timing based on the length of day and night. Animals also have their own circadian rhythms. Owls, bats, and many insects are primarily nocturnal, while many birds rely on light signals for navigation and migration. Humans also have a biological clock that helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle. A lack of this familiar day-night cycle can seriously disrupt physiological functions. Under conditions of drastic temperature and environmental changes, many species struggle to adapt, leading to profound changes in ecosystems. Is the Earth's magnetic field affected? Earth has a magnetic field surrounding it, which helps protect the planet from most of the charged particles from the solar wind. This magnetic field is created by the movement of molten metal, primarily iron, in the Earth's outer core. The convection of conductive material generates electric currents, which in turn sustain the magnetic field through a mechanism known as a geomagnetic dynamo. You may also like The Earth's rotation contributes to the flow of motion in its outer core through the Coriolis effect. Therefore, if the planet were to stop rotating, the mechanism for generating its magnetic field could be affected. However, the extent of change and the sustainability of the magnetic field in this scenario remain uncertain. Earth's core activity also depends on many other factors, including convection and the planet's internal energy sources. Did the Earth really stop spinning? The answer is no, there is no risk of this happening in the near future. In fact, the Earth is slowing down its rotation due to several factors, the most important of which is the tidal force between the Earth and the Moon. According to astronomical calculations, the impact of tides causes the length of a day to increase by an average of about 2.3-2.4 milliseconds per century. This change is very small and imperceptible in daily life. The scenario of Earth ceasing its rotation is therefore primarily a scientific hypothesis that helps researchers understand the role of rotation in climate, the environment, and life. The planet will continue to rotate for a very long time.

articles.cleaned_content: (Dan Tri Newspaper) - If the Earth stopped rotating but continued to orbit the Sun, day and night could last for months, the climate would change drastically, posing major challenges to life on the planet. Astronomer Nikhita Ramkilowan at Rhodes University (South Africa) has provided interesting analyses of this hypothetical scenario. The Earth is like a giant sphere rotating on its axis, completing one revolution in about 24 hours. At the equator, the planet's surface moves at a speed of about 1,670 km/h. Humans don't perceive this movement because their bodies, the atmosphere, and the oceans all move with the Earth. The planet's rotation creates the day-night cycle and influences wind patterns and ocean currents. So what would happen if the Earth gradually slowed down and eventually stopped rotating on its axis, while still continuing to orbit the Sun? Day and night can last for months. If the Earth stopped rotating but continued to orbit the Sun, the day-night cycle at a given location would change dramatically. Instead of alternating between light and darkness every 24 hours, an area might experience about 6 months of light followed by about 6 months of darkness. This scenario doesn't mean half the Earth will permanently face the Sun while the other half remains in darkness. Because the planet continues to orbit the Sun, the regions alternate between illuminated and dark areas. In areas with long daylight hours, the surface absorbs heat for months at a time. Conversely, areas experiencing long nights lose heat, causing temperatures to drop sharply. These temperature differences can profoundly alter the climate and living conditions on the planet. Some areas located near the boundary between light and darkness may maintain relatively more stable light conditions. However, habitability in these areas depends on temperature, water availability, and other environmental factors. Weather and ocean conditions are changing drastically. You may also like The Earth's rotation creates the Coriolis effect, which causes air currents and ocean currents to be deflected as they move across the planet's surface. If the Earth stopped rotating, this effect would fundamentally change. Atmospheric and oceanic circulation systems would no longer function as they do today. Temperature differences between illuminated and long-term shadowed areas can alter wind direction, air circulation intensity, and global heat distribution. As a result, many areas may face extreme weather conditions, far different from the current climate. Life has been turned upside down. Many organisms have evolved to adapt to the day-night cycle. Plants use sunlight for photosynthesis, while some species regulate their flowering and growth timing based on the length of day and night. Animals also have their own circadian rhythms. Owls, bats, and many insects are primarily nocturnal, while many birds rely on light signals for navigation and migration. Humans also have a biological clock that helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle. A lack of this familiar day-night cycle can seriously disrupt physiological functions. Under conditions of drastic temperature and environmental changes, many species struggle to adapt, leading to profound changes in ecosystems. Is the Earth's magnetic field affected? Earth has a magnetic field surrounding it, which helps protect the planet from most of the charged particles from the solar wind. This magnetic field is created by the movement of molten metal, primarily iron, in the Earth's outer core. The convection of conductive material generates electric currents, which in turn sustain the magnetic field through a mechanism known as a geomagnetic dynamo. You may also like The Earth's rotation contributes to the flow of motion in its outer core through the Coriolis effect. Therefore, if the planet were to stop rotating, the mechanism for generating its magnetic field could be affected. However, the extent of change and the sustainability of the magnetic field in this scenario remain uncertain. Earth's core activity also depends on many other factors, including convection and the planet's internal energy sources. Did the Earth really stop spinning? The answer is no, there is no risk of this happening in the near future. In fact, the Earth is slowing down its rotation due to several factors, the most important of which is the tidal force between the Earth and the Moon. According to astronomical calculations, the impact of tides causes the length of a day to increase by an average of about 2.3-2.4 milliseconds per century. This change is very small and imperceptible in daily life. The scenario of Earth ceasing its rotation is therefore primarily a scientific hypothesis that helps researchers understand the role of rotation in climate, the environment, and life. The planet will continue to rotate for a very long time.

articles.title: The Solar System could become unstable, and Earth faces the risk of planetary collision. - Vietnam.vn
articles.author: Báo Tin Tức
articles.content: The Solar System could become unstable, and Earth faces the risk of planetary collision. Small fluctuations in the orbits of planets can upset the balance of the solar system, even putting Earth at risk of colliding with Mercury, Mars, or Venus. According to the Daily Mail (UK), the orbits of planets are not actually fixed but are constantly influenced by each other's gravitational forces. Over billions of years, these interactions can gradually destabilize the solar system. Scientists liken this process to a car wheel becoming misaligned: initially only slightly unbalanced, but over time it can lead to serious problems. When its orbit is disrupted, a planet can be flung out into space, crash into its host star, or collide with another planet. Two French scientists calculated the likelihood of the solar system becoming unstable during the remaining 5 billion years of the Sun's life. The results showed that the gas giants, including Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune, are relatively stable. Meanwhile, smaller rocky planets, including Earth, are more vulnerable to orbital fluctuations. Through 2,501 computer simulations, the research team found approximately 25 cases, or 1%, that could disrupt Mercury's orbit and lead to a potential collision between planets. In one scenario, the orbits of all rocky planets become unstable, leading to the possibility of Mercury, Mars, or Venus colliding with Earth. You may also like Another scenario suggests that Mars and Earth could move so close together that the distance between the two planets is only 794 km. In a paper published in the journal Nature, scientists Jacques Laskar and Mickael Gastineau of the Paris Observatory stated : "An approach this close would have catastrophic consequences for life on Earth. Tidal forces could tear Mars apart, and then the fragments would repeatedly collide with Earth." However, scientists emphasize that these scenarios have a very low probability and, if they do occur, it would still take billions of years. By adjusting some minor parameters in the near-collision scenarios between the two planets, scientists noted several other possibilities. Five scenarios resulted in Mars being ejected from the solar system, while 196 scenarios posed a risk of planetary collision. Notably, in 48 cases, Earth ultimately collided with either Mars or Venus. Commenting on the study in the accompanying article, Dr. Gregory Laughlin of the University of California, Santa Cruz (USA) stated that these findings are not only significant for the Solar System but also contribute to clarifying the formation and transformation of planetary systems around other stars. "With a 99% probability, we can trust in the smooth functioning of celestial bodies. However, the remaining 1% still gives us a sense of potential risks," he stated. You may also like According to Dr. Gregory Laughlin, the question that needs further research is the extent to which chaotic dynamics, even those with only a very small impact on the solar system, have contributed to shaping the number and characteristics of planets throughout the galaxy. However, scientists believe that the likelihood of this scenario occurring is very low, and even if it does, it would likely take billions of years.

articles.title: European-Japanese probe enters orbit of the planet closest to the Sun. - Vietnam.vn
articles.author: Đài truyền hình Việt Nam
articles.content: Although Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun, placing a spacecraft into its orbit presents numerous technical challenges. Due to the strong gravitational pull of the Sun, spacecraft entering the inner regions of the Solar System can reach very high speeds. To be held back by Mercury's relatively weak gravitational pull, the spacecraft must significantly reduce its speed before approaching the planet. Therefore, the BepiColombo mission team designed a complex trajectory, utilizing the gravitational pull of the planets to adjust its orbit and speed. A simulation of Mercury using data from the MESSENGER spacecraft (Image: NASA Goddard) The BepiColombo spacecraft successfully completed its crucial maneuver to enter Mercury's orbit on November 21st, marking a new milestone in its mission to explore the planet. The spacecraft's engines were scheduled to activate at 6:24 PM GMT (1:24 AM on November 22nd in Vietnam time), operating for approximately 37 minutes to adjust its speed and place the spacecraft into orbit. This success makes BepiColombo the second mission to successfully orbit Mercury, following NASA's MESSENGER spacecraft, which orbited the planet between 2011 and 2015. BepiColombo was launched on October 20, 2018, by an Ariane 5 rocket from the Guiana Space Centre in the French overseas territory of South America. This was a large-scale collaborative project between the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), aimed at comprehensively studying one of the most mysterious planets in the Solar System. The mission consisted of two main scientific probes: the Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) developed by ESA and the Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio, built by JAXA. During their journey to Mercury, the two probes were connected to the MTM transport module, which provided power and thrust to propel the entire spacecraft over the long distance through space. Throughout its journey, BepiColombo made one flyby of Earth, two flybys of Venus, and six flybys of Mercury. These maneuvers allowed the spacecraft to gradually reduce its orbital energy without using excessive amounts of fuel. According to the original plan, BepiColombo was expected to reach Mercury about a year earlier than planned. However, a problem with the solar panel system reduced the power supply to the electric propulsion systems of the MTM module, forcing the crew to adjust the itinerary. After overcoming the technical difficulties, the mission proceeded to the most crucial phase: placing the scientific spacecraft into orbit for research. The approach to Mercury began on September 3, 2026, when the MTM transport module separated from the MPO and Mio spacecraft . After entering orbit on November 21, the two spacecraft remained connected for a short time before separating to carry out their own missions. According to plan, Japan's Mio spacecraft will separate from MPO around December 9th and move in an elliptical orbit at an altitude ranging from approximately 500 km to 11,000 km above Mercury's surface. This orbit allows Mio to study the planet's magnetic field and plasma environment, as well as the interaction between Mercury's magnetosphere and the solar wind. Meanwhile, ESA's MPO spacecraft will continue to perform orbital adjustments in the following months. It is expected that by March 10, 2027, MPO will reach its final research orbit, at an altitude of approximately 400-1,500 km above Mercury's surface. Unlike Mio, MPO will focus on studying the planet's surface, chemical composition, internal structure, and geological features. ESA stated that the phase of placing the entire mission into a stable scientific orbit is expected to last approximately six months. Official research activities will begin on April 6, 2027, after the two spacecraft complete the separation and orbital adjustment process. By using two scientific spacecraft operating at different altitudes, BepiColombo is expected to provide complementary data to each other, giving researchers a more comprehensive view of Mercury. One of the mission's key objectives is to understand the origin and characteristics of the planet's magnetic field. Despite its relatively small size, Mercury possesses its own magnetic field. Studying the structure and variations of the magnetosphere could help scientists better understand the physical processes occurring within the planet. In addition, BepiColombo's instruments will survey Mercury's massive iron core, study its surface composition, and learn about the geological history of this planet closest to the Sun. Notably, the Mercury X-ray Spectrometer (MIXS) was used to observe the Crab Nebula, the remnant of a supernova explosion recorded from Earth in 1054. MIXS was the first X-ray imaging instrument to be sent on an interplanetary exploration mission. Testing the instrument during the mission allowed scientists to assess its functionality before beginning the official research program on Mercury. The data obtained is expected to contribute to answering questions about the formation and evolution of Mercury, and to provide more information for understanding the overall history of the Solar System. In particular, studying a planet located near its central star could help scientists better understand the conditions for the formation and evolution of rocky planets in environments heavily influenced by the radiation and gravitational pull of their parent star.

articles.title: Where will NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft go after reaching the one-day mark? - Vietnam.vn
articles.author: Báo Dân trí
articles.content: Where will NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft go after reaching the one-day mark? (Dan Tri Newspaper) - Voyager 1 is expected to continue operating at least until its 50th launch anniversary in 2027, before energy and technical limitations determine the mission's future. NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft has just reached an unprecedented milestone in space exploration history: on November 18th, the spacecraft was approximately 25.9 billion kilometers from Earth, equivalent to the distance light travels in 24 hours, also known as a light-day. This means that radio signals from Earth take approximately 24 hours to reach Voyager 1. The return signal from the spacecraft also takes a similar amount of time to return. Therefore, a two-way communication could last about two days. Since the launch of Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, in 1977, the two probes have made significant surveys of the exoplanets of our Solar System. Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter and Saturn, and also made a close approach to Saturn's moon Titan. Its orbit around Titan moved the spacecraft north of the ecliptic plane, preventing it from continuing its journey to Uranus and Neptune like Voyager 2. Voyager 1 is currently the most distant man-made object from Earth. Meanwhile, Voyager 2 is expected to reach the one-light-day mark in November 2035. So what awaits the two probes as they continue their journey through interstellar space? Interstellar space is the region outside the heliosphere – the area of space created by the Sun's stream of particles and magnetic field. This is the environment that the two Voyager spacecraft are directly surveying, providing unprecedented data about the region outside the influence of the solar wind. Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in August 2012, while Voyager 2 crossed the heliosphere boundary in November 2018. Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), said current research focuses on measuring the strength and direction of magnetic fields, plasma density, and detecting high-energy particles. These measurements help scientists track changes in the interstellar medium as the spacecraft moves further away from the Sun. Linda Spilker, a Voyager project scientist at JPL, said the two spacecraft will continue to monitor the surrounding plasma and magnetic environment, and look for signs that the Sun is still influencing this region of space. "Voyager's primary goal is to determine how far the Sun's influence extends in interstellar space. Where does that influence end, and where does the primordial interstellar space truly begin? Hopefully, Voyager will operate long enough to find the answers," Spilker shared. You may also like The research team also wanted to investigate the relationship between the magnetic field generated by the Sun and the interstellar magnetic field, including changes in the magnetic field direction observed in the area where the spacecraft was operating. Energy management One of the biggest challenges for the Voyager mission is the dwindling power supply. The two spacecraft use radioisotope generators (RTGs), which convert heat from the plutonium decay process into electricity to sustain operation. When launched in 1977, each ship had an electrical power output of approximately 470W. However, this power source decreased by about 4W per year, forcing the operating crew to gradually shut down some equipment to extend its operating time. In early 2026, NASA engineers will perform a power system reconfiguration, shutting down three devices and switching to more energy-efficient options. This solution is expected to keep the remaining scientific instruments on the two spacecraft operational at least until the 50th anniversary of their launch in 2027. According to NASA, the operating team doesn't need to make major changes to its operating procedures before this milestone. However, the remaining power range is very limited, while engineers still need to ensure the temperature of critical components in the extremely cold space environment. Unexpected incidents can also occur. Last October, Voyager 1 lost contact for about 48 hours after NASA's Deep Space Network (DSN) stations failed to pick up signals during two scheduled communications. The spacecraft subsequently restored communication and resumed operations. NASA's goal is not only to maintain connectivity with Voyager but also to extend the operational life of the scientific instruments. According to NASA's instrument status table, Voyager 1 currently has two scientific instruments in operation: the magnetometer and the plasma waveform analyzer. The farther these instruments travel from the heliosphere, the more valuable the data they collect becomes for understanding the interstellar environment. The legacy of Voyager 1 The current Voyager operating team includes multiple generations of engineers and scientists. According to Kareem Badaruddin, mission manager at JPL, younger members like Nshan Kazaryan and Bhavana Gupta are taking on crucial roles, contributing to the mission's future operation. You may also like Kazaryan was responsible for coordinating the connection schedule with the Deep Space Network (DSN), a system of three large antenna clusters located in the US, Spain , and Australia, for communication with probes at long distances. Meanwhile, Gupta participated in systematizing data from Voyager's command and control system and developing troubleshooting manuals. Alongside the younger members are experienced professionals such as Jack Lippincott, who has in-depth knowledge of DSN operations and data analysis. Mr. Badaruddin said that this expert's experience helped the team handle problems that arose at the Goldstone antenna station in California (USA), during a period when the area was affected by extreme weather. Although it is not yet possible to determine how much longer Voyager 1 can operate, the NASA team says they will continue the mission for as long as possible. "It took decades of engineering effort to bring Voyager 1 to the one-day mark. We hope the spacecraft can continue its journey for even longer," Ms. Dodd shared. When it no longer has enough energy to maintain its instruments and communication with Earth, Voyager 1 will continue to drift through space. The spacecraft will not stop at the one-light-day mark but will continue to move further away from the Solar System, carrying the Voyager Golden Disc – a message about Earth that NASA is sending to any civilization that might encounter it in the future.

This means that radio signals from Earth take approximately 24 hours to reach Voyager 1. The return signal from the spacecraft also takes a similar amount of time to return. Therefore, a two-way communication could last about two days.
Since the launch of Voyager 1 and its twin, Voyager 2, in 1977, the two probes have made significant surveys of the exoplanets of our Solar System.
Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter and Saturn, and also made a close approach to Saturn's moon Titan. Its orbit around Titan moved the spacecraft north of the ecliptic plane, preventing it from continuing its journey to Uranus and Neptune like Voyager 2.
Voyager 1 is currently the most distant man-made object from Earth. Meanwhile, Voyager 2 is expected to reach the one-light-day mark in November 2035.
So what awaits the two probes as they continue their journey through interstellar space?
Interstellar space is the region outside the heliosphere – the area of space created by the Sun's stream of particles and magnetic field. This is the environment that the two Voyager spacecraft are directly surveying, providing unprecedented data about the region outside the influence of the solar wind.
Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in August 2012, while Voyager 2 crossed the heliosphere boundary in November 2018.
Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), said current research focuses on measuring the strength and direction of magnetic fields, plasma density, and detecting high-energy particles. These measurements help scientists track changes in the interstellar medium as the spacecraft moves further away from the Sun.
Linda Spilker, a Voyager project scientist at JPL, said the two spacecraft will continue to monitor the surrounding plasma and magnetic environment, and look for signs that the Sun is still influencing this region of space.
"Voyager's primary goal is to determine how far the Sun's influence extends in interstellar space. Where does that influence end, and where does the primordial interstellar space truly begin? Hopefully, Voyager will operate long enough to find the answers," Spilker shared.
You may also like
The research team also wanted to investigate the relationship between the magnetic field generated by the Sun and the interstellar magnetic field, including changes in the magnetic field direction observed in the area where the spacecraft was operating.
Energy management
One of the biggest challenges for the Voyager mission is the dwindling power supply. The two spacecraft use radioisotope generators (RTGs), which convert heat from the plutonium decay process into electricity to sustain operation.
When launched in 1977, each ship had an electrical power output of approximately 470W. However, this power source decreased by about 4W per year, forcing the operating crew to gradually shut down some equipment to extend its operating time.
In early 2026, NASA engineers will perform a power system reconfiguration, shutting down three devices and switching to more energy-efficient options. This solution is expected to keep the remaining scientific instruments on the two spacecraft operational at least until the 50th anniversary of their launch in 2027.
According to NASA, the operating team doesn't need to make major changes to its operating procedures before this milestone. However, the remaining power range is very limited, while engineers still need to ensure the temperature of critical components in the extremely cold space environment.
Unexpected incidents can also occur. Last October, Voyager 1 lost contact for about 48 hours after NASA's Deep Space Network (DSN) stations failed to pick up signals during two scheduled communications. The spacecraft subsequently restored communication and resumed operations.
NASA's goal is not only to maintain connectivity with Voyager but also to extend the operational life of the scientific instruments. According to NASA's instrument status table, Voyager 1 currently has two scientific instruments in operation: the magnetometer and the plasma waveform analyzer.
The farther these instruments travel from the heliosphere, the more valuable the data they collect becomes for understanding the interstellar environment.
The legacy of Voyager 1
The current Voyager operating team includes multiple generations of engineers and scientists. According to Kareem Badaruddin, mission manager at JPL, younger members like Nshan Kazaryan and Bhavana Gupta are taking on crucial roles, contributing to the mission's future operation.
You may also like
Kazaryan was responsible for coordinating the connection schedule with the Deep Space Network (DSN), a system of three large antenna clusters located in the US, Spain , and Australia, for communication with probes at long distances. Meanwhile, Gupta participated in systematizing data from Voyager's command and control system and developing troubleshooting manuals.
Alongside the younger members are experienced professionals such as Jack Lippincott, who has in-depth knowledge of DSN operations and data analysis.
Mr. Badaruddin said that this expert's experience helped the team handle problems that arose at the Goldstone antenna station in California (USA), during a period when the area was affected by extreme weather.
Although it is not yet possible to determine how much longer Voyager 1 can operate, the NASA team says they will continue the mission for as long as possible.
"It took decades of engineering effort to bring Voyager 1 to the one-day mark. We hope the spacecraft can continue its journey for even longer," Ms. Dodd shared.
When it no longer has enough energy to maintain its instruments and communication with Earth, Voyager 1 will continue to drift through space. The spacecraft will not stop at the one-light-day mark but will continue to move further away from the Solar System, carrying the Voyager Golden Disc – a message about Earth that NASA is sending to any civilization that might encounter it in the future.

paragraphs.title: Explanation of zodiac signs in astrology - Báo Nghệ An
paragraphs.paragraph_text: Lý giải về cung hoàng đạo trong chiêm tinh học The zodiac is determined by the position of the Sun in the sky relative to the 12 constellations and is closely related to astrology. | The 12 zodiac signs are linked to the Earth's movement across the sky. Photo: Wordpress. | The zodiac, or the 12 signs listed in astrology, are linked to the Earth's movement across the sky. Because the Earth revolves around the Sun on a plane, we see the Sun appear and move in front of different constellations throughout the year, according to Earth Sky. Just as the Moon appears in a slightly different position in the sky each night, the Sun's position relative to distant background stars gradually shifts eastward from day to day. For example, if the Sun is in Gemini this month, it will be in Cancer next month. The specific dates listed in Western astrology are used to identify when the Sun is in a particular zodiac sign. For example, March 21st to April 19th is the sign of Aries. Nowadays, the zodiac sign you were born in does not necessarily coincide with the name of the constellation the Sun is passing through. To understand why constellations no longer correspond to their respective zodiac signs, we need to know more about how the Earth moves. The Earth rotates, and its North Pole doesn't always point in the same direction. Like a spinning top, the Earth wobbles, causing the North Pole to move in a circle across the celestial sphere. This wobble is quite slow, with a cycle of 26,000 years, meaning the Earth doesn't actually complete a full orbit in a year. After about 2,000 years, the Sun will be in a completely different constellation for the same period of time. On the summer solstice in June 2,000 years ago, the Sun was almost directly between the constellations Gemini and Cancer.

paragraphs.title: Explanation of zodiac signs in astrology - Báo Nghệ An
paragraphs.paragraph_text: But on the summer solstice of 2016, the Sun was between Gemini and Taurus. In the year 4609, the Sun will leave Taurus and move to Aries on the summer solstice. The zodiac signs, corresponding to the constellations through which the Sun passes, were determined 2,000 years ago. However, by the mid-21st century, the slow wobble of the Earth's rotational axis caused the summer solstice, winter solstice, and spring and autumn equinoxes to shift approximately 30 degrees westward relative to the constellations. Currently, the zodiac signs and constellations are out of alignment by about a month. In about 2,000 years, they will be out of alignment by about two months. The constellations of the zodiac are not all the same size and shape. Most of them appear in the texts of the ancient Babylonians and were introduced by Ptolemy, the Greek astronomer who lived in the 2nd century. In 1930, the International Astronomical Union defined the boundaries of modern constellations, encompassing all 13 constellations that lie along the path of the Sun. The constellation not listed in Western astrology is Ophiuchus, located between Sagittarius and Scorpio. According to VNE | RELATED NEWS | |---|

paragraphs.title: Potentially habitable planet near Earth discovered. - Vietnam.vn
paragraphs.paragraph_text: Astronomers have identified a potential candidate for habitable planet, HD 137010 b. This planet orbits a sun-like star and is estimated to be about 6% larger than Earth. Image: NASA. A team of international scientists from Australia, the UK, the US, and Denmark discovered the planet HD 137010 b by examining and analyzing data recorded in 2017 from the K2 expansion mission of the Kepler space telescope of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). Image: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Keith Miller (Caltech/IPAC). Dr. Chelsea Huang, a researcher at the University of Southern Queensland (Australia) and one of the study's co-authors, said that HD 137010 b has an orbital period similar to Earth's, completing one rotation in approximately 355 days. (Image: Eckhard Slawik/Science Photo Library/Getty Images) Researchers predict that planet HD 137010 b has "about a 50% chance of being within the habitable zone" of its central star. Image: NASA/JPL-Caltech. You may also like "What's incredibly interesting about this Earth-sized planet is that its star system is only about 150 light-years from our Solar System," Dr. Huang said. Photo: NASA/JPL-Caltech. According to Dr. Huang, the planet with the greatest potential for extraterrestrial life after HD 137010 b is Kepler-186f. However, Kepler-186f is four times farther away and its central star is 20 times dimmer. Image: NASA/JPL-Caltech. While transiting in front of its central star, the planet HD 137010 b was discovered by a team of citizen scientists, including the lead author of the study, Dr. Alexander Venner, when he was still a high school student. Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, Joseph Olmsted (STScI). "It's truly a wonderful experience to return to this work and make such an important discovery ," Dr. Venner shared.

paragraphs.paragraph_text: Photo: NASA/JPL-Caltech. You may also like The host star of HD 137010 b is cooler and dimmer than the Sun. This means the planet's surface is likely similar to Mars and could have temperatures below -70 degrees Celsius. Image: NASA/JPL-Caltech. paragraphs.title: The mystery of the smallest planet in the Solar System. - Báo Nghệ An
paragraphs.paragraph_text: The mystery of the smallest planet in the Solar System. Mercury is the first planet from the sun, and also the smallest of the eight "siblings" in the Solar System. There are many interesting things about this planet that scientists are currently studying. Mercury is the smallest planet in the Solar System family - Photo: Theosophy online The planet with the most iron in the solar system. Mercury is one of four rocky planets like Earth, and also the smallest, with a diameter of only about 4,879.4 km. This figure is 0.383 times the diameter of the Earth and is even smaller than Jupiter's moon Ganymede and Saturn's moon Titan. Iron makes up a large proportion of Mercury's composition. It is also the planet with the most iron in the Solar System. Along with Venus, Mercury has no natural satellites, while the other planets all have satellites orbiting them. The diurnal temperature range is approximately 600 degrees Celsius. Mercury's atmosphere is extremely thin - Photo: NASA Mercury is also the closest planet to the sun among the eight planets, at a distance of approximately 57.91 million kilometers. This, along with its small mass, makes its atmosphere very thin and unable to retain heat. Therefore, Mercury has the largest diurnal temperature range in the Solar System, with nighttime temperatures dropping to -173°C but daytime temperatures reaching 427°C. This translates to a temperature difference of up to 600°C between day and night. Due to its very thin atmosphere, Mercury does not have seasons like the four seasons on Earth. Mercury's orbit is an extremely narrow ellipse with a major axis radius of 70 million km and a minor axis radius of only 46 million km. This is also one of the reasons for the large temperature differences on Mercury.

paragraphs.title: The mystery of the smallest planet in the Solar System. - Báo Nghệ An
paragraphs.paragraph_text: A day is equal to two-thirds of a year. A year on Mercury is equivalent to only 88 days on Earth - Photo: NASA Mercury orbits the sun at a very fast rate, approximately 88 Earth days. In contrast, Mercury takes about 58 Earth days to rotate on its axis. Thus, a year on Mercury is incredibly fast, only 88 days compared to 365 days on our planet, while a single day is incredibly long, equivalent to about two Earth months. In other words, a day on Mercury is about two-thirds the length of a year. The surface is like the moon. Mercury's surface is uneven, like the moon. Photo: NASA Bề mặt sao Thủy có rất nhiều hố to nhỏ và lởm chởm như bề mặt mặt trăng. Phần lớn bề mặt sao Thủy được dung nham khô bao phủ. Trên bề mặt hành tinh này xuất hiện nhiều vết nứt, hoặc những vách đá khổng lồ kéo dài trên một khu vực rộng lớn, trông giống các nấc thang khổng lồ. Trong đó, nấc lớn nhất dài hơn 1.000km và cao đến 3km. Sao Thủy có lượng lớn miệng núi lửa trên bề mặt hơn bất kỳ hành tinh nào trong Hệ mặt trời. Điều đặc biệt là phần lớn các miệng núi lửa này được đặt tên theo các nhà văn, nghệ sĩ nổi tiếng. "Thần đưa tin" của Hệ mặt trời Thần Hermes trong thần thoại Hy Lạp Con người biết đến sao Thủy từ rất sớm. 3.000 năm TCN, người Sume đã biết có sự hiện diện của sao Thủy. Vì sao Thủy nằm trong quỹ đạo Trái đất nên khi nhìn từ Trái đất chỉ có thể thấy vào rạng sáng hoặc chiều tối chứ không thể thấy vào ban đêm. Người La Mã lấy tên thần Mercurius (người Hi Lạp gọi là thần Hermes) - vị thần liên lạc và đưa tin trong thần thoại, đặt cho sao Thủy. Có lẽ do người La Mã nhận thấy tốc độ nhanh của sao Thủy nên đặt tên như thế. Rất khó "làm quen" Vệ tinh Messenger đã hoàn thành nhiệm vụ vào năm 2015.

paragraphs.title: The mystery of the smallest planet in the Solar System. - Báo Nghệ An
paragraphs.paragraph_text: Ảnh: NASA Our understanding of Mercury remains limited due to the difficulty in accessing the planet. To date, only two probes have attempted to reach Mercury: Mariner 10 in 1974-1975, and Messenger, launched into space on August 3, 2004. As for the Messenger spacecraft, after arriving in Mercury's orbit on March 17, 2011, it carried out the mission of observing and studying the history and geology of the planet, which is closest to the sun. Messenger traveled 7.8 billion kilometers over more than six years to reach Mercury and was the first spacecraft to successfully enter Mercury's orbit. Messenger orbited Mercury from 2011-2015 and sent back more than 280,000 images to Earth before ending its mission by crashing into the planet.

paragraphs.title: Why in the world only 4 countries can produce ballpoint pens? - xaluannews.com
paragraphs.paragraph_text: Ballpoint pens are familiar and common items in our daily lives. The reason why it is called a ballpoint pen is because the nib has a small part that is a ball that has the function of pushing the ink contained in the pen to the outside. A special thing is that almost every country has its own brand of ballpoint pens, but there are only 4 countries in the world that can produce ballpoint pen tips. This ball is small but plays an important role, it rotates freely to allow ink to flow evenly with each pen stroke. Producing a spinning iron ball that can write comfortably for a long time is not a simple thing, but requires a very high level of engineering. Machining accuracy is 1/1000 mm. The error is not allowed to exceed 0.003 mm. Besides the way the small marble is made, the material is also a very important factor. The steel used to manufacture this ball must be a special material - Tungsten carbide has twice the hardness of steel. Therefore, this is also known as one of the most difficult details in the world. Currently, only Switzerland, Germany, Japan and, more recently, China hold the technology of producing ballpoint pen tips. So why in the world only 4 countries can produce this "micro" part? Switzerland and Germany are two rich and developed countries. At the same time, it is famous for its precision, fine and quality machinery manufacturing techniques. Of the four countries, Switzerland is the most "skilled" producer of ballpoint pens.

paragraphs.title: Why in the world only 4 countries can produce ballpoint pens? - xaluannews.com
paragraphs.paragraph_text: The Swiss company takes more than 20 stages to produce a small ballpoint pen with strict requirements: Processing accuracy must reach 1/1000 mm; The tip of the pen has 5 ink channels; The match between the ball, the pen tip and the groove position should not exceed 3 microns, and the thickness at the top of the pen tip is only 0.3-0.4 mm. As an island nation, lacking resources, having to import many things from outside, Japan’s manufacturing industry is very strong and developed, ranked first in the world. With modern scientific and technological applications, ballpoint pens are produced exclusively by Japan throughout Asia. By 2017, China became the fourth country to be able to produce this part. According to China Daily , before that, the country of billions of people produced 38 billion ballpoint pens per year, this number accounts for about 80% of the total number of ballpoint pens in the world. There are more than 3,000 pen manufacturing companies in this country, but none have the advanced technology to produce ballpoint pen tips. Instead, about 90% of the tips are imported from Japan, Germany and Switzerland. According to the China Light Industry Council, this costs the industry $17.3 million a year. After relentless research, China has mastered the ballpoint pen manufacturing technology and now accounts for 80% of the country’s ballpoint pen market. Nearly 40 billion ballpoint pens are produced in a year. In addition to the level of science and technology, the problem of profit also makes few countries invest in the production of this product. The daily output of the iron and steel mill can be equal to the steel consumed by the pen industry in a year. A ballpoint pen on the market can only sell for a few dollars, the profit is not high.

paragraphs.title: Why in the world only 4 countries can produce ballpoint pens? - xaluannews.com
paragraphs.paragraph_text: Therefore, steel mills in many countries are not unable to produce ballpoint pens, but facing the problem of profit, they do not choose to spend money on research and development of this product. Source: General: washingtonpos; craftpaperie; jingdapen

paragraphs.title: A 'second moon' briefly visited Earth. - Vietnam.vn
paragraphs.paragraph_text: Although it may appear to be a "second moon" of Earth, this is not a true satellite. It is expected to escape Earth's gravitational influence in early December 2026 and return to orbit around the Sun. The Minor Planet Center (MPC), an agency of the International Astronomical Union (IAU), said that this asteroid, designated "2026 QQ8", has been held in place by Earth's gravity since April. This asteroid is a small celestial body, with a diameter of only about 2 meters. It is predicted to remain near Earth until early December, before moving out of our planet's gravitational field and returning to its orbit around the Sun. "2026,QQ8" was first discovered last August by Hungarian astronomer Krisztián Sárneczky. Initially, it was thought to be a regular asteroid, but precise orbital calculations have revealed that it is now staying close to Earth. You may also like Analyses indicate there is no risk of collision with Earth. Even if it were to enter the atmosphere, given its small size, it would almost certainly be burned up completely. Such instances, where Earth's gravity temporarily holds a small asteroid in place, are not uncommon. Matthew Payne, director of the Minor Planet Center (MPC), explained: "It is entirely possible that such an object exists near Earth at any given time," adding that they typically remain there for a few weeks or months. You may also like There have been instances in the past where asteroids were temporarily trapped by Earth's gravity. Asteroid 2006 RH120 was near Earth for about a year, while 2020 CD3 orbited our planet for about three years. Astronomers believe that most asteroids observed near Earth originate from the asteroid belt located between Mars and Jupiter.

paragraphs.title: A 'second moon' briefly visited Earth. - Vietnam.vn
paragraphs.paragraph_text: The hypothesis is that the orbits of objects in this belt may be altered by gravitational forces, causing them to move closer to Earth. If their speed decreases sufficiently, they may be temporarily held in place by Earth's gravity. To date, astronomers have identified approximately 40,000 celestial objects in the vicinity of Earth. Across the entire solar system, about 1.5 million celestial objects have been identified.

The planet Kepler-452b orbits a sun-like star and lies within the "habitable zone," where conditions could allow liquid water to exist. Photo: Pinterest. | | 2. It is about 60% larger than Earth. With a diameter about 1.6 times larger than Earth, Kepler-452b belongs to the group of "Super-Earths" – rocky planets with larger masses but still similar conditions to Earth. Photo: Pinterest. | | 3. A year on Kepler-452b lasts 385 days. This planet takes nearly 385 days to complete one orbit around its host star – very close to Earth's 365 days. Photo: Pinterest. | | 4. Its host star – Kepler-452 – is older than the Sun. Kepler-452 is about 10% larger than the Sun and is approximately 6 billion years old – about 1.5 billion years older than the Sun. paragraphs.title: Why will August 2nd, 2027 be the most special day of the 21st century? - Vietnam.vn
paragraphs.paragraph_text: The "eclipse of the century" will occur on August 2, 2027. August 12th will be a highly anticipated day for many astronomy enthusiasts, as it marks the time of a total solar eclipse, when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun, forming a straight line, lasting for 2 minutes and 18 seconds. People living in Vietnam will not be able to observe this phenomenon. Only those living in northern Spain, a small part of Portugal , Iceland, Greenland, etc., will be able to observe the total solar eclipse. Meanwhile, those living in the Northern Hemisphere, including Northern Europe, Canada, and parts of the northern United States, will only be able to observe a partial solar eclipse. A total solar eclipse will not occur again until August 2, 2027. Notably, the eclipse that will happen next year is called the "eclipse of the century," when the Moon will completely obscure the Sun for 6 minutes and 23 seconds, the longest in the 21st century. This time is long enough for the corona (the outermost layer of the Sun's atmosphere) to shine brightly against the dark sky, and the stars will also shine as brightly as they do at night. Scientists say this record will not be broken until June 3, 2114, when a total solar eclipse will last for 6 minutes and 32 seconds. The total solar eclipse in 2027 is one of a series of three total solar eclipses occurring in three consecutive years (August 12, 2026, August 2, 2027, and July 22, 2028). This is also a very rare occurrence. You may also like Why will the total solar eclipse on August 2, 2027 last so long? The reason the total solar eclipse on August 2, 2027, will last longer is because this is when the Moon reaches its perigee, the point in its orbit where it is closest to Earth, making it appear larger when observed from the ground.

paragraphs.title: Why will August 2nd, 2027 be the most special day of the 21st century? - Vietnam.vn
paragraphs.paragraph_text: Coincidentally, at this time, the Earth is also very close to its aphelion, the point where the Earth is farthest from the Sun, so the Sun will be obscured by the Moon for a longer period when observed from the ground. The shadow of the eclipse will also fall on the area near the Earth's equator, where the Earth rotates faster. This makes the eclipse last longer because the Earth's rotation speed catches up with the movement speed of the Moon and the Sun, helping to maintain a straight line between the three celestial bodies for a longer period. Is it possible to observe the solar eclipse on August 2, 2027, from Vietnam? The eclipse path on August 2, 2027, will begin over the Atlantic Ocean, then move across the Strait of Gibraltar, sweeping across southern Spain before moving into North Africa and the Middle East. Countries with the opportunity to observe this total solar eclipse include Spain, Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, and Somalia. Of these, the best location for observing the total solar eclipse for the longest period is the city of Luxor (Egypt). People living in Vietnam will not be able to observe the total solar eclipse on August 2, 2027, but those living in southern provinces and cities such as Ho Chi Minh City, Ca Mau , Can Tho, etc., will be able to observe a partial eclipse, with about 10% of the sun being obscured. However, the eclipse will occur around 6 PM (Vietnam time), making observation difficult. A total solar eclipse is a unique astronomical phenomenon that occurs when the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun, forming a straight line. At this time, the Moon completely obscures the Sun.
